CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up after recent hospitalization for fever, elevated white blood cell count, and concern for urinary tract infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Michelle King is a 39-year-old female with a history of quadriplegia from prior spinal cord injury who was admitted to District Regional Hospital on 06/29/2021 and discharged on 07/02/2021. She presented with increasing spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and diaphoresis. In the emergency department, she was found to be febrile with a white blood cell count of 23,000. She had labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. She was treated with IV antibiotic therapy for concern of urinary tract infection. She has a supra-pubic catheter. Cultures were obtained. She slowly improved and was discharged. 

She presents today for follow-up. Patient reports feeling much better at home after having a substantial bowel movement, which she feels contributed to resolution of her symptoms. She attributes her hospitalization to constipation and autonomic dysreflexia rather than true urinary tract infection. She had not had regular bowel movements during the hospitalization despite daily Miralax use. She notes the weather was extremely hot during the period leading up to admission. She is now back to her normal self.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies current pain or discomfort anywhere. She notes she typically stays inside more during hot weather. She continues to experience constipation despite Miralax use, though she doubles the dose when she does not have bowel movements.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Quadriplegia from prior spinal cord injury
Chronic constipation
Recent urinary tract infection/fever (currently resolved)

MEDICATIONS
Miralax (daily)
Lactulose (as needed for constipation rescue)
Vitamin C supplements
Multivitamins

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient stays indoors during hot, humid weather. She goes outside occasionally. She is unvaccinated for COVID-19. She takes multiple vitamins and supplements. She is somewhat interested in homeopathic approaches.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, normal breathing
General: No acute distress
Abdomen: No pain or discomfort reported

RESULTS
Prior hospitalization labs: WBC 23,000 (elevated), urine cultures not impressive
Recent consideration: White blood cell elevation may be related to dehydration, heat exposure, and constipation-induced inflammation rather than infection

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute to Chronic Constipation: Patient believes hospitalization was related to autonomic dysreflexia and constipation rather than true UTI. She maintains good bowel regimen with Miralax as primary agent and lactulose for breakthrough constipation. Will continue current regimen. Discussed dehydration risk, especially during hot weather. Plan to return in 2-3 weeks for follow-up labs.

2. Leukocytosis: White blood cell count elevation likely secondary to inflammation from constipation and dehydration. Will repeat CBC in 2-3 weeks to ensure normalization. If WBC remains elevated, will investigate for other bowel pathology.

3. Quadriplegia: Chronic condition, stable. Patient managing well.

4. COVID-19 Vaccine Status: Patient currently unvaccinated. Expressed concerns about unknown side effects, reports of vaccine injury, and belief that she is young and healthy enough to fight infection despite limited respiratory status. She takes vitamin C and multivitamins and states she is closely monitored. Physician strongly recommended vaccination given high-risk status from quadriplegia, noting COVID-19 can be severe and has resulted in deaths in his practice, even in previously healthy individuals. Discussed safety profile, noting side effects from all vaccines are rare. Explained that vaccine is only proven preventative mechanism and that supplements are unlikely to provide adequate protection. Patient is somewhat open-minded but hesitant. Encouraged patient to reconsider and to contact office with questions.

5. Fasting Labs: Patient to return in 2-3 weeks for complete blood work including CBC and lipid panel (cholesterol) as she is due for routine screening. This will serve dual purpose of checking white blood cell count and obtaining routine cholesterol monitoring.
